message.content: {"recommended_method":"social_choice","consensus_potential":0.68,"fairness_assessment":"A ranked, criteria-based vote is fairest because the three options represent legitimate but competing user needs; an equal split should not be presumed fair without evidence of demand, costs, and accessibility impacts.","conflict_severity":"medium","stakeholder_analysis":[{"agent":"agent_1","position":"Supports allocating the entire subsidy to expanding the youth book collection.","influence":0.33},{"agent":"agent_2","position":"Supports allocating the entire subsidy to creating a freely accessible computer and digital space.","influence":0.33},{"agent":"agent_3","position":"Supports dividing the subsidy equally between books and the digital space.","influence":0.34}],"recommended_resolution":"collaborative","governance_reasoning":"The debate identifies meaningful tradeoffs rather than irreconcilable interests. Use participatory social choice: gather user-needs and cost data, allow stakeholders to rank options, and select the option with the strongest overall support, potentially refining option C into a needs-based rather than automatically equal allocation."}
